column1: # Format: window <TAB> title <TAB> hook. Lines beginning with # are
# comments, and a comment naming a category applies to everything under it
# until the next one. Read this before running the seed: these 150 subjects
# are the first thing a day-one reader sees, and generating them costs real
# money. Delete, rewrite or reorder freely -- the tool reads whatever is here.

column2: The year with no summer
column3: A volcano in Indonesia froze a New England June.

column2: Why we drive on different sides
column3: Swordsmen, teamsters, and a decision nobody quite made.

column2: The map that ended a cholera outbreak
column3: One pump handle, removed, and a new science.

column2: How standard time was imposed
column3: Railways needed one clock, and towns fought back for years.

column2: The Dutch tulip crash, minus the myth
column3: Most of what you have heard was written by a satirist.

column2: Why the Bronze Age collapsed at once
column3: Eight civilisations, one century, and no single cause.

column2: The telegram that took nine days
column3: News crossed the Atlantic slower than the ships carrying it.

column2: Why ice is slippery
column3: Not pressure, and not friction alone. A liquid layer nobody predicted.

column2: The colour of the sun
column3: It is white. Your sky is what makes it yellow.

column2: Why mirrors reverse left and right
column3: They do not. They reverse front and back.

column2: How GPS corrects for relativity
column3: Satellite clocks run fast; ignoring Einstein breaks navigation within hours.

column2: Why nothing can be perfectly cold
column3: Absolute zero is not merely hard. It is forbidden.

column2: The experiment that weighed the Earth
column3: Two lead balls, a torsion wire, and a shed in Clapham.

column2: Why the sky is not violet
column3: Shorter wavelengths scatter more, so why is it blue?

column2: Why onions make you cry
column3: The plant is defending itself, and it works on you.

column2: Why sourdough never dies
column3: A starter is an ecosystem that defends its own territory.

column2: Your gut has its own nervous system
column3: Five hundred million neurons, deciding things without asking you.

column2: How antlers regrow every single year
column3: The fastest healthy tissue growth in any mammal, on schedule.

column2: Why whales got enormous, and recently
column3: Ice ages concentrated their food, and size followed within millions of years.

column2: The immune system's filing problem
column3: It must remember everything and attack nothing that is you.

column2: Why you have goosebumps
column3: A reflex for fur you no longer have.

column2: Surge pricing before computers
column3: Fish markets solved dynamic pricing a century before anyone else.

column2: Why coins have ridged edges
column3: A defence against a crime that no longer exists.

column2: The price of a rounding error
column3: One index recalculated, and a market moved by billions.

column2: How the shipping container rewrote trade
column3: A standard steel box quietly beat every tariff negotiation of its century.

column2: Why insulin stayed cheap for decades
column3: A patent sold for a dollar, and what happened after it lapsed.

column2: The invention of the weekend
column3: Two days off is younger than the lightbulb, and it was fought for.

column2: The ship that is no longer itself
column3: Replace every plank. Is it still the same ship?

column2: Why you cannot step in the same river
column3: Heraclitus had a point about identity that still bites.

column2: The trolley problem was never about trolleys
column3: Philippa Foot invented it to argue about something else entirely.

column2: Hume's problem with tomorrow
column3: Nothing justifies expecting the future to resemble the past.

column2: What Wittgenstein meant by a game
column3: Some words have no definition, only a family resemblance.

column2: The paradox of the heap
column3: Remove one grain at a time. When does it stop being a heap?

column2: Why Socrates wrote nothing down
column3: His objection to writing survives only because somebody wrote it down.

column2: Why maps put north at the top
column3: It was a choice, and a fairly recent one.

column2: How typefaces steer trust
column3: The same sentence reads as more true in some fonts.

column2: The button that does nothing
column3: Placebo controls on lifts and crossings, and why they stay.

column2: The London Tube map is not a map
column3: Harry Beck drew a circuit diagram and changed how cities are read.

column2: Why hospital signage keeps failing
column3: Wayfinding breaks precisely where people are most frightened.

column2: How the QWERTY story got told wrong
column3: It was not designed to slow you down.

column2: The chair that ruined posture advice
column3: Ergonomics assumed one body, and offices bought millions of them.

column2: Why cathedrals have flying buttresses
column3: The wall is not holding the roof up. Something else is.

column2: The staircase that goes nowhere
column3: A Victorian building quirk that was once a fire code.

column2: How Roman concrete healed itself
column3: Seawater made it stronger, and we only recently worked out why.

column2: Why skyscrapers sway on purpose
column3: A building rigid enough not to move would be ruinous and brittle.

column2: The dome that took a century
column3: Brunelleschi built it with no scaffolding and no surviving plans.

column2: Why old doors are so short
column3: Not shorter people. Heat, timber, and tax.

column2: The city block as an invention
column3: Grid plans are a technology, and they have authors.

column2: Why choirs drift sharp
column3: Group pitch rises predictably, and physics insists on it.

column2: The note that is always out of tune
column3: Every piano you have heard is deliberately, carefully wrong.

column2: How equal temperament won
column3: A compromise nobody liked became the sound of everything.

column2: Why some songs get stuck
column3: Earworms have a measurable shape, and it is not catchiness.

column2: The orchestra seating you hear
column3: Where players sit changes the piece more than the conductor does.

column2: Why a minor chord sounds sad
column3: The interval is physics; the sadness is learned, and not everywhere.

column2: How recording changed performance
column3: Musicians began playing for a microphone, and the playing changed.

column2: Why the frame rate is 24
column3: A sound engineering compromise you have watched your whole life.

column2: The cut your brain refuses to see
column3: Editors exploit a blind spot that lasts a fifth of a second.

column2: The grammar of film cuts
column3: Your brain accepts jumps in space it never actually sees.

column2: How the Hays Code shaped plots
column3: Censorship wrote endings that outlived the censors by decades.

column2: Why films look orange and teal
column3: A colour grading habit, a skin tone, and a complementary shortcut.

column2: Why films are shot out of order
column3: The schedule follows the set, not the story.

column2: The novel that invented the plot twist
column3: Before it, readers were not expected to be fooled.

column2: Why paperbacks changed what was written
column3: Cheap printing did not just move books. It moved sentences.

column2: How the first novel argues about novels
column3: Cervantes was already parodying the form he was inventing.

column2: The translation that made a language
column3: Luther's Bible standardised German more than any government did.

column2: Why nobody wrote about the colour blue
column3: Ancient texts describe a wine-dark sea, and the reason is not eyesight.

column2: The footnote as a joke
column3: Some novels use them to argue with themselves.

column2: Why your knees predict rain
column3: Barometric pressure moves joint fluid just enough to feel.

column2: The memory you are certain about
column3: Confidence and accuracy are almost unrelated, and courts know it.

column2: Why you cannot tickle yourself
column3: Your brain cancels sensations it predicted, a fraction ahead.

column2: How eyewitnesses are made, not found
column3: A line-up is an experiment, and most are badly designed.

column2: The experiments that did not replicate
column3: A decade of psychology was rebuilt after checking its own work.

column2: Why deadlines change what you notice
column3: Scarcity narrows attention in ways that are measurable and expensive.

column2: The star that is not there
column3: Some points of light left before there was anyone to see them.

column2: Why the Moon always shows one face
column3: Tidal locking, and the slow braking that produced it.

column2: How we weighed a black hole
column3: You cannot see it, so you watch what it drags.

column2: The planet found on paper first
column3: Neptune was calculated before anybody pointed a telescope at it.

column2: Why the night sky is dark
column3: It is a harder question than it looks, and the answer is the Big Bang.

column2: Why Pluto was demoted
column3: Not a demotion so much as a discovery about the neighbourhood.

column2: The beach that is mostly parrotfish
column3: Some white sand is not rock. It has been eaten.

column2: Why the Grand Canyon is young
column3: The rock is ancient. The gap is not.

column2: How continents were proved to move
column3: The seafloor kept a magnetic record nobody expected to find.

column2: The flood that carved a landscape in days
column3: An ice dam failed, and Washington State still shows the scars.

column2: Why earthquakes cannot be predicted
column3: Forecasting is possible; prediction may not be, and the difference matters.

column2: Why sand is running out
column3: Desert sand is the wrong shape to build with.

column2: The word that means its own opposite
column3: Cleave, sanction, dust: English contradicts itself on purpose.

column2: Why you say big red barn
column3: Adjective order is a rule you follow and were never taught.

column2: How lost writing systems were deciphered
column3: Linear B, Maya glyphs, and the ones still unread.

column2: The language with no word for left
column3: Some speakers give directions by compass, indoors, in the dark.

column2: Why English spelling is like that
column3: A printing press, a vowel shift, and terrible timing.

column2: Why babies babble the same everywhere
column3: The sounds narrow to a language later than you would think.

column2: Why a shuffled deck is new
column3: That order has almost certainly never existed before.

column2: The birthday coincidence
column3: Twenty-three people, and a better than even chance.

column2: The mathematics of juggling
column3: Siteswap notation turned a circus trick into number theory.

column2: How to be sure without checking
column3: A proof is a promise about infinitely many cases at once.

column2: The map colouring nobody could prove
column3: Four colours, a century of failure, and the first computer proof.

column2: Why zero took so long
column3: A symbol for nothing was a genuinely hard idea.

column2: Why bridges hum
column3: Wind makes steel sing, and engineers tune it out on purpose.

column2: Why tunnels are dug from both ends
column3: Meeting in the middle is a surveying problem, not a digging one.

column2: Why runways get renumbered
column3: Magnetic north drifts, and the paint has to follow it.

column2: How electricity grids stay balanced
column3: Supply must equal demand every second, forever, with no storage.

column2: Why planes are safe
column3: Every rule was written after a crash; the system learns better than people.

column2: The lift that made the skyscraper
column3: Otis did not invent the lift. He invented not falling.

column2: Why paper cuts hurt so much
column3: A shallow wound the body treats as an emergency.

column2: The anaesthetic nobody can explain
column3: We have used it for a century without knowing how it works.

column2: How handwashing was resisted
column3: Semmelweis was right, provably, and it ended his career.

column2: Why placebos still work when disclosed
column3: Told it is a sugar pill, and it helps anyway.

column2: The trial design that changed medicine
column3: Randomisation is a nineteenth-century idea with a body count before it.

column2: Why fever is on your side
column3: Suppressing it is a comfort decision, not always a medical one.

column2: The pigment that poisoned painters
column3: A green so good it was worth the arsenic.

column2: Why old paintings are cracked
column3: The craquelure is a clock, and forgers cannot fake it easily.

column2: How perspective was invented, once
column3: Linear perspective has a date, a city, and an inventor.

column2: The restoration that started a war
column3: Cleaning the Sistine ceiling revealed colours nobody believed.

column2: Why so much sculpture is white
column3: It was painted. Vividly. We inherited the bleached version.

column2: The forger who signed his work
column3: Van Meegeren proved his innocence by proving a worse crime.

column2: The handshake is not universal
column3: Greeting rituals differ so much that neutrality is impossible.

column2: Why we cook
column3: No other animal does it, and our jaws show the consequence.

column2: How agriculture made people shorter
column3: Skeletons record a trade: more calories, worse nutrition, denser settlement.

column2: The gift that must be repaid
column3: Reciprocity is an obligation with rules, not a kindness.

column2: Why every culture has music
column3: It is older than agriculture and possibly older than language.

column2: Why nobody agrees on spice tolerance
column3: Capsaicin sensitivity is partly learned and partly inherited.

column2: The vote that cannot be fair
column3: Arrow proved no ranking system satisfies every reasonable condition.

column2: Why ballots are secret
column3: It was controversial, and the argument against it was not stupid.

column2: How gerrymandering is measured
column3: The efficiency gap turned a smell test into arithmetic.

column2: The census as an instrument of power
column3: Who is counted, and how, decides more than any single election.

column2: Why coalitions form the way they do
column3: Party arithmetic follows rules that were worked out on paper.

column2: Why turnout is measured wrongly
column3: Of registered voters, or of adults? The gap is enormous.

column2: Why bread goes stale in the fridge
column3: Not drying out. Starch retrogradation, and it is reversible.

column2: The reaction that browns everything
column3: Maillard is not caramelisation, and the difference is the flavour.

column2: Why you salt pasta water
column3: Not for the boiling point. The number is trivial.

column2: How pasteurisation was resisted
column3: Milk safety was a political fight before it was a public good.

column2: Why chillies evolved to burn
column3: The heat is aimed at mammals, and birds are exempt on purpose.

column2: The spice trade's real cargo
column3: Preservation is the myth. Status was the business.

column2: Why fermentation was safety before flavour
column3: Preservation came first; taste is what we kept it for.

column2: Why contracts need consideration
column3: A promise alone is not enough, and the reason is old.

column2: The right to remain silent, before Miranda
column3: It existed, and almost nobody knew it did.

column2: How precedent actually binds
column3: Judges distinguish more often than they overrule, and that is the mechanism.

column2: The patent that was sold for a dollar
column3: Deliberate under-pricing as a strategy, and what it cost later.

column2: Why juries decide facts, not law
column3: A division of labour with a violent history behind it.

column2: Why courtrooms have a bar
column3: A literal wooden rail that named an entire profession.

column2: Why passwords have those rules
column3: Most of the advice was one man's guess, and he regrets it.

column2: The bug named after a moth
column3: A real insect, a real logbook, and a misremembered origin.

column2: How undersea cables carry everything
column3: Ninety-nine per cent of intercontinental traffic, in pipes on the seabed.

column2: Why software estimates are always wrong
column3: The bias is structural, measurable, and survives every attempt to fix it.

column2: The compression that throws away sound
column3: MP3 works by modelling what you cannot hear.

column2: Why files have extensions
column3: A three-letter limit from the 1970s still shapes your desktop.

column2: Why leaves change colour
column3: The yellow was there all along, hidden under the green.

column2: The tree that is one organism
column3: A forest of aspens sharing a single root system.

column2: Why flamingos are pink
column3: Diet, not pigment, and a captive flock fades without help.

column2: How migrating birds navigate
column3: Magnetism, stars, and smell, layered as redundant systems.

column2: Why forests need fire
column3: Suppression made the fires worse, and the seeds needed the heat.

column2: The fungus that connects a wood
column3: Trees trade sugar through a network they do not control.

column2: Why deserts get cold at night
column3: No water vapour to hold the day's heat.
